officialApp.name: Zepp
officialApp.notes: Zepp transfers sounds to the buds, sets volume, playback duration/alarm and shows the sleep report. The buds are not a streaming headset.

battery.notes: Official: 12 h in 3-hour playback mode with sleep monitoring all night; 8 h with sound playing continuously. Case adds seven full recharges, quoted as 56 h / eight nights total. Whether Zepp splits left/right and case percentages is not documented.

anc.notes: No ANC. Passive umbrella-shaped tip isolation plus masking sounds; not a noise-cancelling device.

features.name: Downloadable sleep sounds stored on the buds
features.notes: Only Amazfit's official library can be transferred; no Bluetooth streaming.

features.name: Sleep-stage, position and heart-rate tracking
features.notes: Accelerometer plus heart-rate sensing; report in Zepp.

controls.notes: No buttons or touch controls. Playback starts when a bud leaves the case and stops when it returns; volume and track choice are app-only.

audio.notes: Knowles balanced-armature receiver, 20 Hz-8 kHz. Bluetooth 5.0 BLE is used for app sync only; the buds never stream phone audio.

sources.title: Amazfit ZenBuds US launch and battery details

gaps: Battery UI layout in Zepp (split vs combined, case visibility) is not documented.
No official statement on whether the case percentage is live while buds are out.
No codec support because there is no audio streaming.
notes: A sleep-only earplug-style device: BLE for app configuration, sounds stored locally, no calls and no streaming. Included because it is a Bluetooth-connected audio wearable for sleep.
